text: ADOPTED: A SHARED-CRDT WRITE MUST BE AN ATOMIC SWAP, AND THIS ONE BITES SILENTLY. A partially copied JSONL file is STILL VALID JSONL, merely short, so a renderer malformed-line check cannot see it; the actor silently contributes fewer records or none, and the union UNDER-REPORTS WITH NO ERROR. The renderer is not at fault and cannot be fixed - the defect is on the WRITER side. THE FIX: write to a temp file IN THE SAME DIRECTORY and mv it over, which is an atomic rename, so a concurrent reader sees either the whole old file or the whole new file and never a half-written one. Per-actor files need no lock, but they DO need an atomic swap. VERIFY BY RE-READ, NEVER BY cp RETURNING 0. THIS CONVICTS MY OWN METHOD: I used cat >> to append to this very file earlier this tick. text: PEER ADDRESSING IS CASE-SENSITIVE AND THE NODE SEGMENT IS NOT CANONICALISED, SO A HAND-TYPED ADDRESS SILENTLY ADDRESSES A DIFFERENT MAILBOX THAT DOES NOT EXIST. The mailbox directory is <node>%2F<actor>~<hash> and THE HASH IS COMPUTED FROM THE STRING AS TYPED. GAVRIELLA/gavriella.buildkit hashes to 90f7084bfaa5 and exists; gavriella/gavriella.buildkit hashes to b78ccac138aa and does not. Casing is genuinely mixed across the fleet and there is no rule to infer it: GAVRIELLA and ARIELLAS are upper, shiras and olamnit and ariellas are lower, and some actors use a hyphen rather than a dot (shiras-glpnet, olamnit-glpnet). CREDIT WHERE DUE: the client FAILS CLOSED here - exit 4, names the exact path it tried, and says NOT SENT. That is the correct behaviour and the opposite of the doctor verb, which fails OPEN on a vanished root. THE RULE, and I have now broken it twice in two waves: ENUMERATE D:/coop/*~* AND DERIVE THE ADDRESS MECHANICALLY, NEVER HAND-TYPE ONE. A refusal means you typed the name wrong far more often than it means the peer is absent.
